summary.text: A die is a small throwable object with marked sides, used to generate random values in tabletop and other games.
A traditional die is a cube with one to six dots on its faces, and when rolled each value is equally likely.
Dice are very old: ones excavated at the Burnt City in south-eastern Iran are estimated to be from between 2800 and 2500 BCE.

facts.label: Traditional shape
facts.value: A cube with faces marked 1 to 6

facts.label: Loaded dice
facts.value: Designed to favor some results over others

facts.label: Possibly oldest
facts.value: Burnt City, Iran, about 2800 to 2500 BCE

facts.label: Ancient seven rule
facts.value: A Mohenjo-daro die had opposite sides adding to seven

facts.label: Snake eyes
facts.value: A roll of one pip on each die

items.prompt: At a board game you roll a fair standard die. A friend says a 6 is much harder to get than a 3. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, because 6 is the highest value
No, each value is equally likely
Yes, but only on the first throw
No, because 3 comes up more often

items.explain: A rolled standard die shows each value from one to six with equal likelihood.

items.prompt: A casino worker finds a die made to land on some faces more than others, so a cheat can win. What is such a die called?

options.label: A fair die
A polyhedral die
A tali die
A loaded die

items.explain: Loaded dice are designed or modified to favor some results over others, for cheating or entertainment.

items.prompt: In a dice game you throw two dice and both show a single pip. What is that roll nicknamed?

options.label: Snake eyes
Boxcars
Midnight
Tesserae

items.explain: A roll of one pip on each die is called snake eyes; a pair of sixes is boxcars.

items.prompt: Why would a role-playing game ask players to throw dice at all?

options.label: To measure how fast the player can move
To keep score of earlier rounds
To produce a random value
To decide who sits first

items.explain: Dice are used for generating random values in games, including role-playing games and games of chance.

items.prompt: A shop sells a 20-faced die with numerals instead of pips. Does it fail to count as a die?

options.label: Yes, a die must be a cube with pips
It is a die, since dice can have other shapes and numerals
Yes, a die may only have six faces
It is a die only if the numerals are carved out

items.explain: Dice may have other polyhedral shapes and may be marked with numerals or symbols instead of pips.

items.prompt: An archaeologist digs up an ancient terracotta die whose opposite faces each add up to seven. What does that show?

options.label: It is a loaded die made for cheating
It must be a modern copy
It is a Roman die with only four marked sides
An old die already shared a feature of modern dice

items.explain: Terracotta dice from Mohenjo-daro, dated to 2500 to 1900 BCE, included one with opposite sides adding to seven, as in modern dice.
